question: Can any assignment of plaintext letters to the fixed published Naibbe glyph repertoire generate clean Voynich prose when spaces and line boundaries are unconstrained?
scope: Fixed published U/P/S glyph strings. Unknown plaintext mappings may be arbitrary. This does NOT include invented glyph codewords, substitutions of EVA signs, glyph aliases or transcription repairs.
necessary_language: A=U union all pairwise concatenations P S, including ambiguous/rejected combinations; L=A*. Superset of native encryption, including arbitrary table draws and aligned reuse. After arbitrary space deletion words are in L; after arbitrary boundary insertions and line truncation every contiguous observed line must be a factor of L.
algorithm: Epsilon NFA with separate U/P/S tries, root→Uroot orProot, Uterm→root, Pterm→Sroot, Sterm→root. Closed start=root, accept root. Open start=ALL reachable/coaccessible states, accept any nonempty final state. Assert every state is reachable and coaccessible.
parsing: All non-! prose loci kind[1]==P in ZL and IT. Replace <-> with dot; remove other angle metadata; trim whitespace. Retain a line only when all remaining characters are lowercase a-z, dot or comma and at least one letter. Exclude entire uncertain lines; never delete an unknown sign and join its neighbors. Split dot/comma for diagnostic tokens; concatenate all clean tokens for line tests.
reports: closed line segmentation in A* after removing all separators
open line factor of A* allowing truncated first/last atoms
primary: Open line compatibility, most permissive. At least one verified counterexample invalidates an error-free full-corpus reading within this fixed glyph family, regardless of unknown letter key. Report acceptance and exclusions, not percent decoded.
certificates: For each rejected open line, find first prefix with empty active state, then shortest suffix of that prefix still rejected. Record locus, start/end EVA indices, factor and whether factor uses only codebook alphabet. Verify factor rejected and its proper one-character prefix/suffix accepted.
controls: All A atoms accepted closed; every nonempty substring of every atom accepted open; all archived phase1 generated ciphertext lines accepted closed/open. Positive long concatenations with all possible cuts in bounded deterministic examples; small toy grammar exhaustive negatives. Independent explicit-dictionary segmentation/factor DP. No language model or plaintext values used in classifier.
known_control: Archived phase1 Greshko-generated Pliny ciphertext, with known tables. Reused solely as parser positive control; not a fresh unknown-key calibration.
decision: If primary has counterexamples, do not run unknown plaintext-key search under unchanged repertoire as a decipherment of the complete manuscript. Passing would only permit further key work, not validate meaning. No failing case deleted after results.
historical_status: Naibbe is modern Greshko construction with period-compatible materials, not an established historical cipher used for Voynich.
prior_difference: Phase1 addendum tested fixed maps at supplied token boundaries, compound disabled. Here key-independent support, unlimited concatenation and open line ends; no new alphabet inferred.
limits: Transcription errors, allographs and alternative codeword inventories remain outside this family. ZL/IT correlated, corpus exposed; clean subset excludes uncertain lines. Constraint is structural, not evidence of absence of meaning.
